cost: THE ROUND IS 93 AND THE PIPELINE IS 96. recal_95 shipped at PIPELINE_VERSION 95 while this round was on Tomer's desk, so 93 could not ship as 93 without going backwards. Both python files carry 96 and this file's `pipeline_version` is 96 — the receipt checks the SHIPPED version, not the round number. A later reader should not expect round N to equal pipeline N from here on.

ONE OF THE FIVE RULINGS IS DECLINED and rolls forward. "Ty Jerome '25 OFF should be high 60's to mid 70's. Not 81" (off 71 +-4) is NOT in data/anchors.json, on recal_91's precedent: an anchor is a pin that HOLDS, and this one does not. It is recorded here with its measurement and belongs in anchors.json the round that lands it.

WHY IT IS INFEASIBLE, and this one is a PROOF rather than a search. The blocker is MONTREZL HARRELL '18, recal_52's own anchor: OFF 77 +-1 earned in 17.0 mpg — a SMALLER load than Ty Jerome '25's 19.9 on every measure there is (1,292 season minutes to 1,393; 11.0 ppg to 12.5; usage 23.8 to 23.6; BPM 3.3 to 4.3). Before the round Harrell reads 76.96 and Jerome 80.86 on the same scale. The two rulings together require Harrell >= 76 and Jerome <= 75 — that is, the transform must INVERT them. But any load term T(score, load) that is non-decreasing in BOTH arguments (more score out for more score in, more score out for more load — which every discount toward a bench footprint is, multiplicative, additive or a ceiling alike) satisfies T(76.96, 17.0) <= T(80.86, 19.9). No such term exists. It is not a matter of parameters.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY REACHABLE, measured on the whole pool. Sweeping a minutes ramp (lo, hi, depth) with every standing anchor required to pass: the largest discount that breaks NOTHING moves Ty Jerome '25 81 -> 80, one point, and Harrell 77 -> 76. Push it far enough to reach the top of his band (75) and SEVEN anchors break at once — Harrell '18 by 6, Steve Kerr '96 (23.4 mpg, 62 +-1) by 5, Tony Snell '18, Clint Capela '17 and '18, and at greater depth Korver '15, Hachimura '26, Anunoby '21 and SGA '25. The closest reachable value is therefore OFF 80.

THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME CONFLICT, which only he can settle. His fifth ruling contradicts HIS OWN recal_78 ruling, which pinned Ty Jerome '25 at off 82 +-2 — the pin the card currently satisfies at 81. That anchor is LEFT IN PLACE and still passes, because it is the ruling that holds on the shipped data and doctrine says he decides which of two rulings stands, not the agent. If he confirms the new number, r78's pin moves to anchors_superseded.json and the load question comes back with Harrell '18 reopened alongside it — those two must be answered together or not at all.

THE SEAM THIS ROUND CREATES, stated plainly. is_big is UNCHANGED. Only d_score's branch is now a weight; the boolean still labels the card (p['big']), still gates recal_55's big hub and recal_91's stretch-big floor inside o_score, still splits the marginal percentile classes, and still chooses the OVR cap branch. So Andre Iguodala '14 is now graded on defence as the wing he is, while still being LABELLED a big and still taking the big's o_ovr+40 cap. Nothing currently reads wrong because of it, but a later round that wants the label fixed must change is_big itself, and that WILL move OFF and the cap — which is precisely why this round did not.

THE TACTICS BANDS THIS ROUND BROKE, and the standing procedure that answers them. The harness draws its random fives from PLAYERS with ovr >= 55, so any round that moves OVR moves the SAMPLE. This one moved 683 OVRs on the merged pool and THREE taxes broke at once — the most in any single round — and on BOTH edges: scheme (oracle +0.498 against the +0.50 floor), crashDef (oracle +0.455), and hunt (blind -0.255 against the -0.30 floor). Per the law's own instruction ("tune them ONLY through it") and the precedent of recal_67/72/78/80/85/86/89/91/92, all three were re-ratified through the harness rather than the ratings being bent: scheme .90 -> .60, crashDef .75 -> .40, hunt 3.60 -> 3.70. crashOff held at .50 untouched. Two came DOWN and one went UP in the same round, which is the first time that has happened. RECORD FOR THE NEXT ROUND: hunt's feasible window on this pool is only 3.66-3.78 — twelve thousandths wide — and it has now moved in five of the last six rounds; expect to re-ratify it again and do not read the movement as instability in the tactic. crashDef is the other one to watch: r92 RAISED it .68 -> .75 to answer a blind edge, and this pool moves its ORACLE edge instead, so it comes back down past where r92 found it.

THE CAP IS STILL A CAP. It binds on 532 perimeter cards after the change (813 before) and still pulls Kawhi Leonard '14 DOWN from his 83 blend to 80. recal 3's offence gate — o_ovr + 10 — is untouched, which is the half that governs every perimeter card whose defence is ordinary. What moved is only the elite-defence FLOOR, which is what was actually deciding the subject.

THE OLDER RECEIPTS THIS ROUND TURNS RED, named rather than left to be found. All three are knobs this round deliberately moved: recal_23's and recal_37's "the offence-gates-ceiling cap + big exemption stands, unchanged" (both regex the literal `0.80 * d_ovr`, which his "Kawhi 14 agree" amends — both blocks already carried a note saying two of their three ratified modifiers had been superseded by recal_85, and this is the third), and recal_62's "re-ratified taxes" (which regexes `scheme: 0.90`, re-ratified here through the harness exactly as r67/72/78/80/85/86/89/91/92 each re-ratified one). Additionally the `PIPELINE_VERSION = N` knob lines of rounds 91, 92 and 95 now miss, which is what every version bump has done to its predecessors for seventy rounds. recal_92's own tax knob also misses now (it regexes crashDef 0.75, which this round re-ratified to 0.40 through the harness on the merged pool) - exactly as recal_91's crashDef knob was superseded by recal_92 one round earlier. Nothing was rewritten to hide any of it: a hand-written block is the record, not a thing a later round edits.

MAGIC JOHNSON IS THE LARGEST UNASKED-FOR MOVE, and it should be looked at before anything else. Eight of his seasons rise 9 to 14 points on DEF ('86 63 -> 75, '88 63 -> 77, '89 67 -> 80) because he is listed at every position from PG to C, so the position branches cannot decide him and he fell through to the shape clause. Under the cliff a 6'9" point guard with rim 60+ and no three was graded as a rim protector on rimprot in the 40s; under the ramp he is graded mostly on perdef, like the perimeter defender he was. The direction is right and the anchors all hold, but nobody ruled on it.

SUPERSEDED WITHIN THIS ROUND'S OWN LIFETIME, recorded rather than quietly dropped. Before the rebase onto recal_92 and recal_95, this round measured its collateral against recal_91's attributes and re-ratified TAX.scheme .90 -> .62 there. That measurement is VOID: the merged pool is a different sample, and every number in this file — the movers, the top 12, the tax constants — was re-taken from scratch on the merged data with the sweep starting from origin/main's constants, not from .62. The four LANDED targets and the declined one are unchanged to the point: 90 / 85 / 76 / 80 / 81, identical on both bases, because recal_92 and recal_95 moved neither rimprot nor perdef nor 3pt nor rim on any of the five cards or on Scottie Pippen '94, the ramp's tightest constraint.

A PIPELINE-SYNC FACT FOUND DURING THE REBASE, now moot but worth the line. Rebasing first onto 22356fb (recal_92 alone), a clean run of THAT commit's own build_ratings.py did not reproduce THAT commit's own shipped attributes: rimprot differed on 1,549 cards. Rebasing onto 13bde1b (recal_92 + recal_95) it reproduces EXACTLY — zero attributes and zero talents differ. So r92's commit shipped data that already contained r95's rim-ceiling change while its code did not yet, and r95 landing closed the gap. Nothing to do now; the check is worth repeating at the head of any future rebase, because a round that regenerates on a commit in that state would silently ship a different board.

SEVEN RANK FLIPS TOUCH THE TOP 50 BY OVR ON THE MERGED BOARD, where the pre-rebase measurement had zero, and they are ONE event rather than seven. NO card already in the top 50 changed its OVR at all. LeBron James '07 goes 92 -> 93 and INSERTS above six cards, each of which slides down exactly one place; Dwyane Wade '09 is displaced from 50 to 51 at an unchanged OVR 92. The 19-place jump the scout prints (rank 64 -> 45) is a TIE-CLUSTER artefact and not a reordering: 22 cards share OVR 92 and 11 share 93, so one point carries him over the whole block. He is the dispatch's own stated exception — a card that was clearly clipped: 3pt 39, ONE point under the `3pt < 40` cliff, routed through the big d_score mix on rimprot 74 against perdef 82, which read him at DEF 86 in a career line of 84/86/94/95/94. He now reads 90. The round did this on recal_91's attributes too (92 -> 93 there as well); what changed is only that the merged board's tie block sits differently, so the same +1 now crosses the 50th line. NOTHING WAS TUNED to avoid it and DEF_RP_LO was not touched — reported for Tomer, per the dispatch.

STANDING ON THIS ROUND, and NOT resolved here: recal_97 ("This is 99 per def. 3+ dpbm. Perfect heigh. perfect voting") removed three ceilings from perdef's VOTED band, and every card with a full-vote sheet rose with Michael Jordan. Three lines in this receipt are red because of it and are LEFT red on purpose, so the conflict is visible where the ruling lives: THE SUBJECT, Andre Iguodala '14 def, target 88 +-3, reads 93; Andre Iguodala '15 def 88 -> 91; Gary Payton '96 def 86 -> 88. All three are drep-1.00 defenders. Their anchors were moved to anchors_superseded.json by recal_97 with a PENDING TOMER note. They cannot be held without reopening recal_97, because holding them means putting the ceiling back on Jordan — Tomer decides which ruling stands, not the agents. Everything else in this round is untouched: the defence-branch ramp, the elite-defence floor and the declined load term are all as shipped.
notes: WHAT THE FIRST THREE RULINGS ARE ABOUT, in one sentence: is_big's middle shape clause reads a SHOT DIET. `rim` and `3pt` are the offensive zone ratings o_score sorts as z[0..2], so how a man SCORED was choosing which of two very different formulas graded his DEFENCE — and the two formulas are 15 to 23 printed points apart. Andre Iguodala '14 took the big mix, whose largest term is 0.40 x rim protection, on rimprot 39.

WHY A RAMP AND NOT A BETTER CLIFF. His dispatch asked that both be measured, and they were, over the whole (threshold, slack) grid. Branching from DEFENSIVE SHAPE as a cliff (rimprot against perdef) reads Scottie Pippen '03 at either 70 — still a big — or 79, and never 75-77, because a cliff can only ever return one of the two formulas. Worse, every setting that routes '03 to the perimeter also routes Scottie Pippen '94 there, and his r80 anchor of 92 +-1 breaks at 96. The two Pippens are the proof: '94 at rimprot 74 must STAY a big, '03 at rimprot 56 must land between the two, and no threshold on any single quantity separates them. Only a blend can produce a number that is not one of the two formulas.

WHY THESE FOUR CONSTANTS. Every one is the clause's own. The ramp on rim protection tops out at 80, which IS the third clause's "an elite deterrent is a big whatever his shape" bar — so that clause stops being a separate cliff and becomes this ramp's ceiling. The fade runs from the clause's own `3pt < 40` line down to 30. The bottom of the rimprot ramp, 45, is the only free number, and it is set by the measurement: 45 is the widest foot that keeps Pippen '94 at 93 while bringing '03 to 76. The 3pt half is load-bearing and not decoration — without it Kawhi Leonard '17 (rimprot 60) becomes half a big and his 95 +-1 anchor breaks at 91.

NO GENUINE BIG MOVES, measured rather than claimed, on the merged board. The position branches are untouched, so all 4,307 cards decided by "PF or C and never a guard" have d_bigness exactly 1.0 and identical arithmetic; the same holds for every lifetime guard at 0.0. Zero of the 4,307 moved. The 220 movers are all cards the POSITION rules could not decide — SF-only men and the mixed guard-and-big listings — which is exactly the population the shape clause exists for.

DEFECT B, DECOMPOSED BEFORE IT WAS CHANGED. Kawhi Leonard '14 blends to 83 and printed 76. The binding term was NOT the offence gate (o_ovr + 10 = 75) but the elite-defence FLOOR, 0.80 x 95 = 76 — so the round loosens exactly the half that decided him. Two alternatives that also reach 80 were measured and rejected: widening the gap to o_ovr + 15 (613 cards move, max +5) and a defence-proportional gap o_ovr + 10 + 0.17 x (d - o) (584, max +4). Both rewrite the offence gate for every perimeter card on the board, including the ones whose defence is ordinary and whose cap was never the complaint.

MEASURED BEFORE APPLYING, on the whole pool, each defect separately and then combined — and RE-MEASURED from scratch on the merged recal_92 + recal_95 board after the rebase; these are the merged numbers. DEFECT A alone: DEF moves on 220 of 10,000 (max +20 Andre Iguodala '14, max -8 Dominique Wilkins '97, mean signed +1.75), OVR on 174, OFF on 0. DEFECT B alone: OVR on 541, every one of them UP because a cap can only be loosened, max +5; DEF and OFF on 0. COMBINED: DEF 220, OVR 683 (mean signed +2.19), OFF 0, attributes 0. The cap decided 739 perimeter cards before and decides 433 after. All 100 anchors pass.

THE SEQUENCES THE SCOUT FLAGGED, after. Iguodala '13/'14/'15 reads 93/90/88 where it read 93/70/88. Butler '15/'16/'17 reads 89/85/83 where it read 89/71/83. That is the whole claim of the round: a career is a curve, and a one-point move in a shooting rating should not put a step in it.

REBASED ONTO recal_92 AND recal_95, and the round survives them without a constant changing. Those two rounds rewrote perdef (the r16 DFG floor retired, the tracked diff regressed to reliability 0.345) and rimprot (the no-vote rim ceiling graded by blocks x DBPM) — the two attributes this round's ramp and both d_score vectors are built on, so the exposure was real and was checked card by card. It moved NEITHER on the five subjects nor on Scottie Pippen '94: Iguodala '14 rimprot 39 / perdef 92, Butler '16 51 / 84, Pippen '03 56 / 74, Pippen '94 74 / 94, Kawhi '14 66 / 92, Kawhi '17 60 / 93 — identical before and after. DEF_RP_LO stays 45 and DEF_3P_LO/HI stay 30/40; nothing was retuned to hold a target.
